ObjectName.value: Cooling Lava of Volcanic Eruption on Heimaey in Iceland - 1973-08-20 2233 - NASA Nighttime Aerial Thermograph

Categories.value: Aerial photographs of Iceland|PD NASA|Thermal images|Heimaey eruption 1973|Volcanology in Iceland|Lava of Vestmannaeyjar

ImageDescription.value: Vertical aerial thermograph taken on August 20, 1973, at 2233 hrs UT of the island of Heimaey, Vestmannaeyjar, Iceland, showing the thermal emission from joints and fissures in the cooling lava (about 6 weeks after the end of the volcanic eruption). The cooling, but still hot, lava glows white in this image.

Credit.value: https://pubs.usgs.gov/gip/heimaey/heimaey.pdf Image was published in a USGS General Interest Publication: Richard S. Williams, Jr., and James G. Moore (1983) "Man Against Volcano: The Eruption on Heimaey, Vestmannaeyjar, Iceland", 2nd edition, page 21.

ImageDescription.value: Final steps of the descent towards Heimaey Airport, Iceland, approx 1 minute before landing. Roughly the northwestern 20% of the island of Heimaey are visible. On the left, behind the low cliffs of the western coast, Vestmann's golf course and behind it the island's camping at the bottom of Herjólfsdalur and mount Blátindur. On the center, one's can see the main sportfield, with the port and mount Heimaklettur just behind. The city of Heimaey covers all the rightern part of the picture, bordered behind by Eldfellshraun, lava flows from 1973 eruption. Further away, the small islands of Elliðaey and Bjarnarey (upper right) are also seen.
